title.rendered: News: Morningdew Media has released JORNA, a hybrid synth workstation combining wavetable, granular, multisample and physically modeled pluck synthesis.

content.rendered:
Morningdew Media has launched version 1.7 of JORNA, its hybrid synth workstation for macOS. The instrument combines wavetable, granular, multisample and physically modelled pluck synthesis within a single plugin environment.

JORNA is designed to allow its four synthesis engines to operate simultaneously on each voice. Users can cross-modulate the engines, while the instrument provides editors for multisamples, wavetables and MSEG shapes.

The workstation includes more than 46 stereo filter types and a 32-lane modulation matrix for assigning modulation sources and destinations. Morningdew Media also includes MUTATOR and PLUCK macros, which are intended for adjusting transient characteristics and morphing parameters.

JORNA supports MPE-compatible controllers and includes an integrated piano-roll sequencer. Its interface uses GPU acceleration, according to the developer.

Version 1.7 adds AAX support for Pro Tools on Mac, extending JORNA’s available plugin formats. The update also introduces expanded granular synthesis features, although Morningdew Media has not specified the individual additions.

JORNA is available in CLAP, VST3 and AU formats, with AAX now available for Pro Tools on macOS.

JORNA has a regular price of €99 and is currently listed at €59. Morningdew Media has not stated an end date for the offer.

title.rendered: News: Segment CPH has released Palora, a polyphonic virtual-analog synthesizer.

content.rendered:
Segment CPH has launched Palora, a polyphonic virtual-analog synthesizer for macOS and Windows. The new instrument is the first plugin from the Copenhagen-based developer and is available in VST3, AU and standalone formats.

Palora is a subtractive synthesizer designed to cover a range of electronic music sound types within a single instrument. Segment CPH describes its design as combining a straightforward workflow with features for building plucks, basses, pads, leads, keys, stabs and drones.

The instrument provides 16 voices of polyphony, with a mono mode and up to four unison copies per voice. Its sound engine includes two morphing oscillators, each able to move continuously between saw, triangle and sine waveforms, alongside pulse wave and PWM options. Additional sound sources include a sub oscillator and a per-note click layer, which can use noise, FM or a sub-body sound.

A four-pole ladder filter offers two selectable characters from the same controls. The Analog mode is described as warm and self-saturating, while the Modern mode is intended to provide a cleaner filter response. Each voice also includes its own transient shaper, allowing the attack and sustain characteristics to be adjusted independently for individual notes.

  • An 11-by-24 modulation matrix with 264 simultaneous routings.
  • Modulation sources including three LFOs, an additional envelope, per-note randomisation, two macros, velocity, key tracking, mod wheel and aftertouch.
  • Live visual feedback for modulation routes.
  • An arpeggiator and step sequencer with up to 24 steps, tempo synchronisation and swing.

Palora also includes a five-stage effects chain comprising Drive, stereo Chorus, stereo Delay, Reverb and output EQ. The Drive effect provides Warm, Soft, Hard and Wild modes, while the reverb section includes Room, Hall, Plate and Spring types.

The plugin ships with 310 factory presets, plus an Init preset. Segment CPH has grouped the supplied sounds into Pluck, Bass, Pad, Lead, Keys, Stab and Drone categories, and presets can be auditioned while browsing.

Palora uses an open, human-readable preset format intended to make it possible to create and share presets. Segment CPH states that this format can also be used by an AI assistant to generate an individual preset or a preset collection from a plain-language description. According to founder Peter Bojesen, many of the included factory presets began as AI-generated designs before being refined manually.

MIDI Learn is available for most controls, and Palora responds to MIDI velocity, mod wheel, aftertouch, pitch bend and sustain pedal data. Activation takes place offline, without an account or iLok requirement.

Palora is priced at €79. Segment CPH is offering a 40% launch reduction, bringing the price to €47.40. A full-featured 14-day trial is also available.

title.rendered: News: Mock Band has refreshed Mock Band, an online practice accompaniment app for drums, bass and chords.

content.rendered:
Mock Band has refreshed Mock Band, its browser-based practice accompaniment application for drums, bass and chords. The updated version is designed to provide editable backing setups for instrumental practice, with recorded acoustic drum sounds, synthesised rhythm guitar and controls for adjusting arrangements while playing.

Mock Band is hosted online and can be used in a web browser without creating an account or downloading software. It is designed as an accompaniment tool rather than a plugin, DAW, native mobile application, AI song generator, or source of note-for-note song transcriptions.

The application combines drum, bass and chord parts in editable practice arrangements. Users can load a setup containing four sections, then change between those sections at the next bar during playback. Controls are available for tempo, key, time signature, swing and drum fills.

The refresh includes setups intended for styles and rhythmic approaches including galloping metal, doom, death metal and progressive 7/8 grooves. These setups can be edited to suit an individual practice session rather than functioning as fixed recordings.

Mock Band provides both on-screen controls and text commands. Optional voice and MIDI control are also supported where the user’s browser and device provide the required compatibility. The original synthesised drum kit remains available in situations where the recorded drum sounds cannot be loaded.

The September update adds shareable setup links and five-minute genre-focused practice guides. Opening a shared setup link allows the recipient to inspect its settings, while explicit Load and Start actions are required before playback begins. Shared links do not automatically start audio or overwrite a user’s saved scenes.

The hosted version of Mock Band is currently free to use. Its source code is private.

title.rendered: News: The Very Loud Indeed Co. has released Songbird: Dark Flute Explorations, a solo flute sound library for Kontakt.

content.rendered:
The Very Loud Indeed Co. has launched Songbird: Dark Flute Explorations, a solo flute library for the full version of Native Instruments Kontakt. The release forms part of the developer’s Dark Explorations series, which is designed for creating atmospheric material associated with thriller, dark drama, and horror contexts.

Songbird: Dark Flute Explorations features recordings by symphonic flautist Natalia Trigueros. The library focuses on extended and unconventional flute sounds, with the performer exploring a range of techniques intended to produce tense and unsettling textures.

The library contains 337 sound files recorded at 24-bit/48 kHz resolution. Its installed size is 1.1 GB, and it provides five primary articulations:

  • Long
  • Short
  • Flutter
  • Trill
  • Key Clicks, presented as percussive elements

Songbird: Dark Flute Explorations includes a Kontakt interface designed to provide direct access to the available sounds and articulations. The instrument requires the full version of Kontakt 7 or later and is not compatible with the free Kontakt Player.

System requirements include macOS 10.13 or later with an Intel i5 processor, or Windows 7 or later with an Intel i5 or equivalent processor. The library also requires graphics hardware supporting OpenGL 2.1 or later, 6 GB of RAM, and 1.1 GB of available storage space.

Songbird: Dark Flute Explorations is priced at $79.00 and is currently available for $49.00, representing a 38% discount. No end date for the offer has been specified.

title.rendered: News: ZAK Sound has released Atmospheres 2, a free reverb plugin that creates spaces from text prompts.

content.rendered:
ZAK Sound has launched Atmospheres 2, a reverb plug-in that generates reverb textures from written text prompts. The free plug-in is designed to let users describe an imagined place, material, or feeling, then apply the resulting atmosphere to incoming audio.

Atmospheres 2 uses prompts to guide the character of its generated reverb spaces. Users can enter their own descriptions, with ZAK Sound noting that English prompts are intended to provide the best results. The process runs locally on the device, without requiring an account, cloud connection, or online activation.

The plug-in also includes a Random function for generating a phrase and a corresponding reverb space. According to ZAK Sound, using Random does not alter the current Mix setting, allowing users to browse generated atmospheres while retaining their existing wet/dry balance.

A central Mix control adjusts the balance between the original signal and the generated reverb. This provides a single control for setting how prominently the generated atmosphere is heard in the processed signal.

Atmospheres 2 combines its prompt-generated textures with water-inspired reverb processing derived from ZAK Sound’s Deep Waters 2. The two layers are blended automatically as part of the plug-in’s generated atmosphere process.

Generated atmosphere settings and the Mix value are stored within compatible DAW projects. This means that reopening a session, or duplicating an instance of the plug-in within a project, retains the associated atmosphere and mix configuration.

Atmospheres 2 is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux. An AUv3 version compatible with iPhone and iPad is also available through the Apple App Store.

ZAK Sound Atmospheres 2 is free to download and use.

title.rendered: News: Snorkel Audio Releases v1.1 Update for Snorkel Synth Plugin Featuring New Melody Generation Engine.

content.rendered:
Snorkel Audio has launched version 1.1 of Snorkel, its generative synthesizer plugin for Windows and macOS. The update introduces a new Melody Generation Engine, expanding the plugin’s tools for creating melodic material from chord progressions.

Snorkel is designed as a generative instrument for developing musical ideas through editable patterns, chords, arpeggios, melodies, synthesis and sequencing. According to Snorkel Audio, the software provides parameter randomisation while allowing users to adjust each generated result manually.

The new Melody Generation Engine creates a single melodic line over a song’s chords. It joins the plugin’s existing Chords module, which generates chord material and includes a built-in gater effect, as well as a grid-based 16-step Patterns sequencer.

Snorkel’s feature set also includes the following modules:

  • An arpeggiator with adjustable controls for generating arpeggiated parts.
  • A Step Modulator for creating parameter modulation.
  • A synthesizer section with three oscillators, a noise source, dual filters, effects, EQ, four LFOs and envelopes.
  • A sequencer for combining generated and programmed elements into a complete musical arrangement.

The plugin is available for Windows, macOS and iPad. Snorkel Audio states that user feedback is welcome as development of the product continues.

Snorkel is currently available for €29 as part of a 50% introductory discount. The offer is listed as expiring on September 13.

title.rendered: News: Orchestral Tools releases Splinter experimental string ensemble library for the free SINE Player.

content.rendered:
Orchestral Tools has launched Splinter, an experimental string ensemble library for its free SINE Player. The library combines chamber strings with electronic, acoustic, and processed instrumental elements, recorded at Saal3 in Berlin’s Funkhaus complex.

Splinter is built around a small string ensemble comprising two violins, two violas, two celli, double bass, and tutti patches. Orchestral Tools describes the collection as focusing on extended and alternative playing techniques, including performance details, incidental noises, and other physical characteristics of the instruments.

The library also includes an Ondes Martenot, with palm speaker and effects material, alongside selectable legato styles. Additional instruments include a detuned upright piano, drum kit, assorted percussion, toy percussion, scrapyard percussion, electric guitar, bass guitar, and banjo.

Several of the non-string instruments were recorded using unconventional approaches. These include bowed guitar and alternative techniques for stringed instruments. Splinter also provides playable glissandi that can be controlled with the mod wheel.

The sound design section contains 50 multi-layered patches intended for further processing and arrangement work. Orchestral Tools positions the collection for composers and sound designers working with contemporary scoring, experimental instrumental textures, and arrangements that combine acoustic sources with designed sound.

  • Experimental chamber string ensemble with individual and tutti instruments
  • Ondes Martenot, detuned upright piano, drum kit, percussion, guitar, bass, and banjo
  • 50 multi-layered sound design patches
  • Up to 11 microphone positions
  • Separate reverb chamber channel

Splinter was recorded at Saal3, Funkhaus Berlin, a room originally designed for chamber ensemble recordings. The library includes multiple microphone positions, with up to 11 available depending on the instrument or patch. A vintage echo chamber from the facility is provided as a separate channel, allowing its reverb contribution to be adjusted independently.

The library runs in the free SINE Player.

Splinter is priced at €299.00, with an introductory price of €199.00 until October 7, 2026.

title.rendered: News: Acon Digital launches Acoustica 8 audio editing and mastering suite.

content.rendered:
Acon Digital has launched Acoustica 8, an audio editing, restoration and mastering suite for Windows and macOS. The Acoustica 8 range comprises standalone software alongside a suite of audio plugins, with editions designed for editing, repair, mixing and mastering workflows.

Acoustica 8 is intended to cover audio work including restoration, spectral editing, multitrack production and final mastering within one application. Acon Digital states that the software can be used for music production, post-production and content-creation projects, with tools for repairing, isolating, editing and processing audio.

The Standard Edition includes spectral and stereo clip editing, multitrack editing, restoration tools and mastering functions. It also supports ARA integration for use with compatible DAWs.

The Premium Edition expands the software’s channel-format support to immersive audio projects up to 7.1.2. It additionally includes Restoration Suite 2, Mix & Mastering Suite, Drum Production Suite and Extract:Dialogue 2.

The Ultimate Edition bundles Acoustica Premium with support for formats up to 9.1.6, along with DeVerberate 3, Verberate Immersive and DeFilter. This edition is positioned for sessions requiring the included immersive processing and additional restoration tools.

Acoustica 8 is available for 64-bit Windows and macOS systems. The Windows version requires Windows 10 or 11, an Intel Core i5 or AMD Ryzen 5 multi-core processor or faster, at least 4 GB of RAM, 10 GB of free disk space, and a display resolution of 1920 × 1080 or higher. Plugin use on Windows requires a compatible 64-bit VST3 or AAX host, with Pro Tools 2021 or later specified for AAX support.

On macOS, Acoustica 8 requires macOS 12 Monterey or later, at least 4 GB of RAM and 10 GB of free disk space. The Mac plugin formats are AU, VST3 and AAX, with Pro Tools 2021 or later required for AAX compatibility.

A 30-day trial is available without a credit card, and Acon Digital provides a user guide for the software. Existing Acoustica 7 owners are eligible for upgrade pricing. Customers who purchased Acoustica 7 after August 1, 2026, receive a free upgrade to the corresponding Acoustica 8 edition.

Acon Digital is offering a 25% introductory discount on new Acoustica 8 licences and upgrades until October 6. Acoustica Standard Edition 8.x is available for US$112, reduced from US$149; Acoustica Premium Edition 8.x is US$224, reduced from US$299; and Acoustica Ultimate Edition 8.x is US$337, reduced from US$449.

title.rendered: News: Rocksolid Audio launches TEQ-6P EQ plugin for Win and Mac in Standard and Unique editions.

content.rendered:
Rocksolid Audio has launched TEQ-6P, an EQ plug-in for macOS and Windows available in Standard and Unique editions. The plug-in uses a virtual circuit design in which individual electronic components are modelled and connected to represent the signal path of a hardware unit.

TEQ-6P is designed around component-level circuit simulation. According to Rocksolid Audio, the signal is processed through modelled resistors, capacitors, coils, valves, and transformers in real time, with the components wired together as part of the virtual circuit.

The plug-in includes three valve styles and three transformer styles, alongside auto gain and oversampling options. It also provides classic and modern interface styles, and is compatible with Rocksolid Audio hardware.

Rocksolid Audio offers TEQ-6P in two licensing and component-tolerance configurations:

  • Standard Edition: Includes one machine licence and standard modelled component tolerances.
  • Unique Edition: Includes three machine licences, unlimited licence transfers, and resale eligibility. Each licence is assigned an individual serial number and a separately randomised set of component tolerances.

For the Unique Edition, Rocksolid Audio states that the varying tolerances represent small differences between electronic parts within an individual unit. This gives each licensed instance its own component configuration rather than using the same tolerance values across all copies.

TEQ-6P is provided in VST3, AU, and AAX formats for macOS and Windows. Supported operating systems range from macOS 13 through macOS 26, and from Windows 10 through Windows 11.

The stated system requirements include 2 GB of RAM and a display resolution of at least 1440 × 900 pixels or 1280 × 960 pixels.

Rocksolid Audio is offering a 60% introductory discount on both TEQ-6P editions with the code INTRO60. The expiry date for the offer has not been specified.

ProjectSAM has launched version 1.1 of Lineage Strings, its Kontakt Player library for string ensemble writing. The update is available at no additional cost to existing Lineage Strings users and introduces changes to legato behaviour and articulation detection.

Lineage Strings is based on recordings of a 35-player string ensemble made at the Broadcasting Music Center in Hilversum, the Netherlands. The library is designed for composers creating string arrangements, with tools intended to support connected melodic lines, articulation selection, and ensemble arranging.

Version 1.1 includes improved legato and enhanced articulation detection. ProjectSAM has not detailed further individual changes within these areas, but the update is provided free to current owners.

The library provides up to 13 articulations for each string section and has an installed library size of 151 GB. Its performance and arrangement features include:

  • Smart Lookahead
  • Adaptive Phrasing
  • Intelligent Arranging and The Arranger
  • Polyphonic Legato
  • Precision Control and automatic vibrato
  • Full bowing control
  • Accessibility options

Lineage Strings supports both the NKS1 and NKS2 standards. This provides access to essential library functions and parameters from compatible NKS hardware, including Native Instruments Komplete Kontrol controllers.

ProjectSAM has also stated that a Free Edition of Lineage Strings is in development.

title.rendered: News: Scaler Music unveils Scaler EQ Pro expanded musical equalizer plugin.

content.rendered:
Scaler Music has launched Scaler EQ Pro, an expanded version of its musical equalizer plugin. The new release retains the key-aware Harmonic Peak filter concept of Scaler EQ while adding revised filter architecture, MIDI-controlled EQ functions, and dedicated compression tools.

Scaler EQ Pro is designed to apply equalization in relation to a selected musical scale. Its Harmonic Peak filters can be configured so that boosts affect frequencies associated with notes within the selected key, while cuts affect frequencies outside that key. This behaviour can also be reversed.

The plugin includes a Detect function that analyses incoming audio to identify a musical scale, using the scale-detection technology also used in Scaler 3. Users can store up to three keys for sessions requiring key changes. A piano keyboard display shows the notes being boosted or cut, while individual notes can be added or removed to create custom scales.

Alongside Harmonic Peak filters, Scaler EQ Pro provides conventional EQ band types, including standard shelf and peak filters, high-pass and low-pass filters, Flat Tilt, and Tilt Shelf filters.

The new Live Band mode enables MIDI control over the plugin’s harmonic EQ filters. When MIDI is routed to Scaler EQ Pro, played notes create filter bands corresponding to notes in the selected scale. Single MIDI notes can be used to control individual bands, while polyphonic MIDI can activate multiple bands simultaneously. Note velocity and ADSR settings determine the strength and response of the bands.

Scaler EQ Pro also includes Magic Shelf filters, retained from the previous version. These are designed to apply different amounts of processing to mid and side information. The low shelf increases mid content more than side content, while the high shelf increases side content more than mid content. The same proportional relationship applies when cutting.

Dynamics processing has been expanded with separate bass and high-frequency compressors. In addition, any EQ band can be switched to dynamic operation, including Harmonic Peak filters. Dynamic band controls include:

  • Threshold
  • Ratio
  • Attack
  • Release

Dynamic bands can be set up for compression or expansion by applying positive or negative gain values to the selected band.

Scaler EQ Pro is available now in VST, AU, and AAX formats for PC and Mac for $99. Existing Scaler EQ version 1 owners can upgrade for $29. Upgrades are available through scalermusic.com, including for users who purchased their Scaler EQ licence elsewhere.

title.rendered: News: Voidscan Audio debuts Parasite three-operator auto-patch-generating FM synth plugin.

content.rendered:
Voidscan Audio has launched Parasite, a three-operator FM synthesizer plugin with auto-patch generation, modulation tools, effects, and a step gate. The instrument is designed around a compact main interface, with additional parameters available through its Advanced section.

Parasite uses three FM operators and provides six algorithms for routing them. Its primary sound-shaping controls include Vortex and Helix for adjusting harmonic ratios, Plasma for scaling modulator levels, and Time for changing the overall speed of a patch. Drive and Fold are included as distortion-oriented processing controls, while each effect can be enabled or disabled independently.

The central visual element is described by Voidscan Audio as a raymarched object connected to the synthesizer voice, which changes in response to playback. The interface places the main performance and sound-design controls around this display, while less frequently used settings are accessed from the Advanced button.

The plugin includes three drawable LFOs, each with eight assignment slots. These can be routed across 64 destinations, including parameters such as filter cutoff, reverb size, and delay time. Modulation assignments are made by selecting an LFO slot and then selecting the target control.

Parasite’s effects and processing chain operate per voice, allowing individual notes in chords to be processed separately. Alongside more conventional effect parameters, the plugin includes two controls called Liquid and Rubber, described as materials that move the sound towards their respective behaviours. A 32-step gate is positioned after the reverb stage and can process the completed signal, including reverb tails.

For patch creation, Parasite offers an automatic patch-generation function intended to create complete sounds rather than independently randomising each parameter. The Mutate control applies this generation process by a selectable amount, allowing users to move an existing patch towards a newly generated variation. Parameters can be locked before mutation to retain selected elements of a sound.

The factory library contains 153 presets across the following categories:

  • Bass, lead, pluck, keys, pad, and texture
  • Drums and FX, which account for 66 presets in the library

Preset browsing supports category, pack, favourite, and text-name filtering. Users can also send a created preset to another Parasite user from within the plugin. Preset packs can be built through the user dashboard and are available across the user’s machines.

Parasite is available for €59 until 23 October, after which it will be priced at €89.

title.rendered: News: MG Music has released MG Ukuleles, a ukulele sample library featuring sampled soprano and baritone ukuleles.

content.rendered:
MG Music has launched MG Ukuleles, a Kontakt sample library featuring sampled soprano and baritone ukuleles. The instrument is designed to provide both direct melodic performance and pattern-based chord and rhythm creation within Kontakt.

MG Ukuleles includes two instruments with different pitch ranges and tonal characteristics. The soprano model is intended for the familiar higher-register ukulele sound, while the baritone model provides a lower register with a more guitar-like character. Users can switch between the two models from the instrument interface.

The baritone ukulele also includes an alternative DI signal, which can be used with the library’s built-in amplifier modules. Both instruments include close and far microphone positions, with controls for balancing the signals and adjusting stereo width.

The Perform section is designed for real-time keyboard playing, including melodic parts, chords, strums, arpeggios and single-string hits. Keyswitches provide access to articulations including slurs, slides, legato, vibrato, palm mutes and bends.

MG Music states that the library uses up to seven round robins and four dynamic layers per note. Its string-selection system is intended to select strings according to typical ukulele playing behaviour. Overlapping notes within the specified legato range can trigger hammer-ons and pull-offs, while velocity influences their response.

Additional performance noises, including string squeaks, shifts and slides, are available via keyswitches. Fret noise can also be configured to trigger when the sustain pedal is released, with manual control available for users who wish to place these sounds directly.

The chord and strum system supports triad-based chord input. Auto mode identifies major, minor, seventh and suspended chord voicings, while Manual mode allows users to create their own voicings. Strum speed and humanisation controls are included for strummed and arpeggiated performances.

The library also includes a sequencer for building rhythmic chord and arpeggio patterns. It provides four banks with up to 32 steps each, and users can determine individual string activity, articulations, strum direction and relative step volume.

  • Preset ukulele patterns and user-created sequences can be saved and reloaded.
  • Sequence controls include bar length, time signature, step rate, strum speed, swing and humanisation settings.
  • Recorded chord changes and performances can be dragged from the sequencer into a DAW as MIDI data.

A Calibrate page provides controls for overall volume, stereo width, microphone balance, fret-noise level, compression and note attack. It also includes a Double Tracking feature with width and performance-tightness controls.

The FX page includes convolution reverb, algorithmic reverb and delay. Three amplifier options are also provided, with the alternative baritone DI signal intended for use with these processing modules.

MG Ukuleles is available from the MG Music website for £75.00, with a limited-time introductory price of £58.44.

title.rendered: News: Audiofier releases Overflow layered cinematic sound design instrument for Kontakt.

content.rendered:
Audiofier has launched Overflow, a cinematic sound-design instrument for Kontakt. The instrument combines organic recorded sources with processed layers, designed to create evolving textures, drones, particles, and other playable hybrid sounds.

Overflow is structured around a main sound layer and two processed companion layers. Users can blend and reshape these elements through controls for tuning, panning, filtering, randomisation, and other playback parameters.

The instrument includes 113 multi-sampled sound sources, organised as 32 main instruments and 81 processed Longs, Echoes, and Shorts. Audiofier describes the source material as drawing on organic sounds alongside processed echoes, unstable textures, and evolving movement.

The three processed material collections are intended for different types of sound behaviour:

  • Longs provide sustained and evolving transformations.
  • Echoes introduce repeated movement and textural tails.
  • Shorts contain transient material, fractured details, and short gestures.

Overflow includes a randomisation function that can generate new combinations of source material, processing layers, movement, playback behaviour, sends, and effects. The feature is designed to provide changing starting points while retaining the instrument’s layered structure.

For more detailed editing, the Advanced page provides direct access to layer selection, sample start position and length, playback probability, voice limiting, pan motion, release, filtering, reverb, delay, and modulation. Layers may also be selected individually rather than through randomised combinations.

Audiofier positions Overflow for composers and sound designers working with expressive textures and organic, processed detail. Its sound palette is designed to cover quieter ambient material as well as more tense cinematic sound-design applications.

Overflow is available from the Audiofier website for $79, with an introductory price of $69.

title.rendered: News: CRQL has released Crumpets, an audio plugin for separating and shifting formant and harmonic content.

content.rendered:
CRQL has launched Crumpets, an audio plugin designed to separate and shift formant and harmonic content within an audio signal. The plugin uses cepstral processing to provide independent control over these elements, including separate adjustment of mid and side formant information.

The name Crumpets is an anagram of “cepstrum”, referring to the signal-processing domain used by the plugin. A cepstrum can be described as the spectrum of a spectrum, and can be used to distinguish characteristics associated with a sound’s spectral envelope, or formants, from its harmonic structure.

According to CRQL, Crumpets processes incoming audio into formant and harmonic cepstra. These are transformed back into frequency-domain components, allowing the formant shape to be adjusted before the signals are shifted, re-convolved, and returned to the time domain. The process is intended to work with polyphonic formant material.

Crumpets provides a cepstrum display in which formants are shown in orange and harmonics in blue. Its main controls include:

  • Res, which sets the cepstral cutoff used to separate formant and harmonic information.
  • Mid and Side, for shifting formant information in the corresponding mid and side channels.
  • Mix, providing a dry/wet balance from 0 to 100 percent.
  • Gate, which controls cepstral gating on the input signal.

The plugin also includes Auto mode for monophonic cepstrum cutoff tracking, along with MIDI control of the cepstrum cutoff. A Lock function links the Mid and Side shift controls so that both channels can be adjusted together.

Crumpets is available from the CRQL website for £13.00.

title.rendered: News: 13x Audio has released AURORA, a free 24-band dynamic EQ plugin for mixing, mastering and tonal shaping.

content.rendered:
13x Audio has launched AURORA, a 24-band dynamic EQ plugin for mixing, mastering and tonal shaping. The current release, version 1.4, updates compatibility, Smart Ops audio capture, Linux editor stability and the plugin workspace.

AURORA provides up to 24 parametric EQ bands, with dynamics available on each band. Its interface includes a live spectrum analyser and direct curve editing, allowing bands to be created and adjusted from the displayed frequency response.

The plugin supports stereo, mid/side and left/right placement for individual bands. Processing modes include zero-latency, natural and linear phase options, while Clean, Subtle and Warm settings provide alternative character modes.

AURORA also includes Smart Ops, a set of analysis-based tools designed to create editable EQ bands from incoming audio. The available operations cover several common EQ tasks:

  • Matching a reference spectrum
  • Identifying and reducing resonances
  • De-essing
  • Unmasking competing tracks

Bands generated by Smart Ops remain standard AURORA EQ bands and can be adjusted manually after they are created.

According to 13x Audio, version 1.4 was shaped largely by feedback received following the initial release. The update restores compatibility with macOS 11 and later, including a fix for a loading issue affecting macOS 13 and macOS 14. It also revises Smart Ops audio capture, improves editor stability on Linux and introduces a refined workspace.

AURORA is available for Windows 10 and Windows 11 in VST3 and CLAP formats. The macOS version supports macOS 11 or later and is supplied as a universal build for Apple Silicon and Intel systems, with AU, VST3 and CLAP formats available. Linux x86_64 support is provided in VST3, CLAP and LV2 formats.

AURORA is available as a free download, with no account, licence key or trial period required.

title.rendered: News: All the Machines has released The Remnant, a drone synthesizer plugin built around eight interconnected FM voices.

content.rendered:
All The Machines has launched The Remnant, a drone synthesizer plugin for macOS and Windows. The instrument is built around eight interconnected FM voices and is available in VST3, AU, and CLAP formats.

The Remnant is an original instrument inspired by the SOMA Lyra-8, while using its own synthesis structure and control approach. Its sound engine centres on eight FM voices connected through a feedback matrix.

Each voice can modulate any other voice in the system. According to All The Machines, this interconnected routing allows the sound to continue changing over time without continuous parameter adjustments. The relationships between the voices serve as the primary method for shaping the instrument’s output.

The plugin includes snapshots, which store the complete state of the synthesizer. Users can glide between snapshots to transition from one configuration of the instrument to another.

Four acoustic filters are provided to shape the output signal. The Remnant also includes 13 scales, intended to keep drone material within selected musical pitch relationships when required.

An iOS version of The Remnant has also been submitted to Apple and is currently awaiting review.

The Remnant is available now for $19 from all-the-machines.com.

title.rendered: News: prod. Shane has released Shane Tune, a vocal note editor with separate pitch, timing, formant and level controls.

content.rendered:
prod. Shane has launched Shane Tune, a vocal note editor for macOS and Windows with individual pitch, timing, formant, and level controls. The new plug-in is part of a range of seven audio tools from the Korea-based producer and developer, available in VST3, AU, and AAX formats.

Shane Tune displays vocal material as editable note blobs. Users can drag, cut, glue, and stretch notes, with pitch, timing, formant, and level parameters available independently for each note.

According to prod. Shane, the plug-in identifies notes using an optimal segmentation process rather than a greedy approach. This is intended to divide held notes and pitch slides at the points where the detected pitch settles. Pitch shifting is handled through time-domain PSOLA processing, with fractional placement of epochs.

The plug-in can also be used across multiple vocal takes. A second Shane Tune instance can align a double or triple vocal track to a lead take. Instances use the host’s absolute timeline, allowing the aligned track to inherit the same warp as the main edit.

Alongside Shane Tune, prod. Shane’s current range includes six other plug-ins:

  • Shane Autotune is a real-time pitch-correction plug-in with separate note-selection and correction-reference controls. It also includes a harmony macro that follows the corrected note.
  • Shane DS is a de-esser featuring a split mode designed to reduce the sibilant band while retaining the vowel signal, alongside a constant-reduction mode.
  • Shane Multi is a four-band compressor with spectrum-based draggable crossover points. Its phase-compensated split design is intended to provide a flat sum when all bands are bypassed, and its Dynamic EQ mode uses bell-shaped filters rather than bands.
  • Shane 73 combines console preamp and EQ functions. Its drive section uses transformer saturation, with the stated behaviour of low frequencies distorting before higher frequencies.
  • Shane CX is a digital synthesizer built with operators rather than samples. It provides 32 front-panel programs and an additional operator page for deeper editing.
  • Shane Moogybass is a monophonic bass synthesizer based around a ladder filter. Its filter envelope is designed to discharge in the manner of an RC network.

All seven plug-ins are supplied in VST3, AU, and AAX formats. The macOS versions are Universal binaries that are signed and notarised, while Windows versions are 64-bit. Each paid plug-in includes a seven-day trial period that begins when that individual plug-in is first opened, with trial periods tracked separately for each title.

Shane Tune is available now for $49. The remaining listed plug-ins are priced from $25 to $35, with the range available from prod. Shane’s Gumroad store.

title.rendered: News: Carbon Fiber Plugins has released La Taconuda, a physical modeling plate reverb plugin.

content.rendered:
Carbon Fiber Plugins has launched La Taconuda, a physical modelling plate reverb plugin designed to simulate resonant metal structures. The plugin offers 12 plate-based structures and controls intended to range from compact plate-style reverbs to extended metallic resonance and drone-oriented effects.

La Taconuda uses physical modelling rather than static impulse responses. According to Carbon Fiber Plugins, incoming transients dynamically excite the modelled metal surfaces, allowing the reverb response to change in relation to the input signal.

The plugin includes six resonant alloy types and parameters for adjusting the behaviour of each plate. Its controls cover plate dimensions, material thickness and tension, alongside stereo pickup microphone placement. These settings are intended to shape the resonance, decay and stereo presentation of the generated reverb.

La Taconuda provides two interface modes. Play Mode presents a reduced set of macro controls for quicker adjustment during tracking, mixing or stem printing. The available controls are Drive, Decay, Width, Tone and Mix.

Advanced Mode provides access to the plugin’s physical modelling and processing parameters, including:

  • Plate size, thickness and tension controls
  • Adjustable stereo pickup microphone positions
  • Ducking for managing the reverb signal alongside lead material
  • Pre-filtering and a three-band tone EQ

Carbon Fiber Plugins states that the wider parameter ranges can also be used for sound-design applications, including sustained metallic textures and unconventional resonant effects. The product’s name references La Taconuda, a figure from Nicaraguan oral folklore associated with the resonant sound of high heels on streets and stone surfaces.

La Taconuda is priced at $85. Carbon Fiber Plugins is offering a launch price of $59 until November 2.

title.rendered: News: AvBo Plugins has released Echo Pitch, an app and plugin combining multi-tap delay with real-time pitch shifting for Mac.

content.rendered:
AvBo Plugins has launched Echo Pitch, a delay and pitch-shifting application and plugin for Mac and iOS. The software combines a multi-tap delay engine with real-time pitch shifting, allowing pitch transposition to be applied to successive delay repeats.

Echo Pitch is designed to create delay patterns in which echoes can rise or fall in pitch over time. According to AvBo Plugins, individual repeats can be transposed to produce cascading pitch trails for uses including ambient textures, harmonised loops, and evolving delay effects within a DAW or compatible host.

The multi-delay engine supports multiple delay voices, enabling layered rhythmic and ambient patterns. Its pitch-shifted feedback function applies transposition across delay repeats, while a Harmonizer mode adds tuned intervals to the incoming signal.

Echo Pitch is available as a standalone application and in plugin formats for supported platforms:

  • Mac: standalone app, VST3 plugin, and Audio Unit v3 plugin.
  • iOS: standalone app and Audio Unit v3 plugin for compatible AUv3 hosts.

The Mac plugin formats are intended for use in VST3- and AUv3-compatible DAWs, while the iOS version can be used in compatible AUv3 host applications.

Echo Pitch is priced at $14.99.
